description: Multi-arm arm selection: the same study label carries different Ns across analyses. A1.1 uses analysed-participant Ns of the biggest-dose exercise arm; A1.3 uses randomised denominators and pools comparator arms. Examples (A1.1 exercise/control N -> A1.3 n/N): Klein 1985 14/8 -> 15/27 vs 16/24; Fremont 1987 18/16 -> 18/21 vs 31/40; Veale 1992 36/29 -> 36/48 vs 29/35; Williams 2008 17/12 -> 15/16 vs 20/22; Blumenthal 2012a control 21 -> 23/24; Krogh 2009 exercise 48 completers -> 48/55 randomised; also Blumenthal 1999 is 55 vs 48 in 1.1 but 53 vs 48 (mean 8.2 vs 8.7) in 4.1. Review states biggest-'dose' arm used for 10 multi-arm trials (smallest-dose version = Analysis 6.7)
note: printed cells themselves are KNOWN/verbatim; which arms were pooled into each A1.3 cell is not stated at the plot and is AMBIGUOUS from the plots alone (both passes agree)

description: Cross-analysis arm reuse between Analysis 1.3 and Analysis 2.2: Fremont 1987 'Control' 31/40 in A1.3 is numerically identical to the 'Cognitive therapy' arm in Analysis 2.2; Klein 1985's 15/27 vs 16/24 also appears identically in Analysis 2.2 — comparator arms double-counted across comparisons

Blumenthal 1999 follow-up cells (Analysis 1.2) print Mean(SD) '10.6 (0.8)' / '11 (0.8)' — SDs an order of magnitude smaller than the same trial's post-treatment SDs (6.9/6.5); values look like SEs from the companion publication (Babyak 2000) deposited as SDs. Printed CI (-1.03 to 0.02) is consistent with the printed cells
note: SD-vs-SE suspicion cannot be resolved from this PDF; recorded verbatim and flagged (both passes); not corrected
